title: Development and Production Configurations knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Development and Production Configurations”?
options: Development and Production Configurations removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Development and Production Configurations should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Development and Production Configurations helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Development and Production Configurations means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
questions.answer_key: Development and Production Configurations helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Development and Production Configurations is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Development build settings” in this lesson?
options: Use “Development build settings” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Development build settings” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Development build settings” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Development build settings” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Development build settings” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Development build settings” under Development and Production Configurations. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Development and Production Configurations”?
options: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
